title: SOON: Symmetric Orthogonal Operator Network for Global Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Climate Forecasting
abstract: Accurate global Subseasonal-to-Seasonal (S2S) climate forecasting is critical for disaster preparedness and resource management, yet it remains challenging due to chaotic atmospheric dynamics. Existing models predominantly treat atmospheric fields as isotropic images, conflating the distinct physical processes of zonal wave propagation and meridional transport, and leading to suboptimal modeling of anisotropic dynamics. In this paper, we propose the Symmetric Orthogonal Operator Network (SOON) for global S2S climate forecasting. It couples: (1) an Anisotropic Embedding strategy that tokenizes the global grid into latitudinal rings, preserving the integrity of zonal periodic structures; and (2) a stack of SOON Blocks that models the alternating interaction of Zonal and Meridional Operators via a symmetric decomposition, structurally mitigating discretization errors inherent in long-term integration. Extensive experiments on the Earth Reanalysis 5 dataset demonstrate that SOON establishes a new state-of-the-art, significantly outperforming existing methods in both forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency.
problem: Existing Subseasonal-to-Seasonal forecasting models treat atmospheric fields as isotropic images, which conflates distinct physical processes like zonal wave propagation and meridional transport, leading to suboptimal modeling of anisotropic dynamics and rapid error accumulation.
method: We propose the Symmetric Orthogonal Operator Network (SOON), which couples an anisotropic embedding strategy that tokenizes the grid into latitudinal rings with a symmetric decomposition of Zonal and Meridional Operators to model distinct atmospheric dynamics for S2S climate forecasting.
task: The task is to perform global Subseasonal-to-Seasonal (S2S) climate forecasting by predicting bi-weekly atmospheric conditions for weeks 3-4 and 5-6 in advance, using a novel neural network designed to model anisotropic atmospheric dynamics.
innovation: This paper proposes the Symmetric Orthogonal Operator Network (SOON) for S2S climate forecasting, which explicitly decouples zonal and meridional dynamics using an anisotropic embedding strategy and a symmetric operator splitting scheme to improve accuracy and computational efficiency.

The framework is composed of three strategic modules: (i) Anisotropic Embedding, which projects the global grid into a sequence of latitudinal ring tokens by compressing longitudinal spatial information into feature channels; (ii) A stack of Symmetric Operator Blocks (SOON Blocks), which function as high-order neural solvers via a symmetric Strang splitting scheme, explicitly employing a Zonal Operator to capture global spectral wave dynamics and a Meridional Operator to model local spatial transport; (iii) A lightweight Decoder, which projects the evolved latent representations back to the physical space to generate the final bi-weekly forecasts.

Dataset. Consistent with the established benchmarking protocols (Liu et al., 2025a;b; Lyu et al., 2026), we evaluate SOON on the ERA5 reanalysis dataset (Hersbach et al., 2020), which is widely used as a reference for global atmospheric fields. We regrid the data to a 1.5° resolution, resulting in a 121 × 240 latitude-longitude grid. Following (Liu et al., 2025a;b), we use 63 variables in total. This includes six pressure-level variables (geopotential z, specific humidity q, temperature t, u-wind u, v-wind v, and vertical velocity w) at ten pressure levels (10, 50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 700, 850, 925, and 1000 hPa), as well as three surface variables (2-meter temperature t2m, 10-meter u-wind u10, and 10-meter v-wind v10).
